units: Kidd. 70ᵃ ס׳ דאמור רבנן וכ׳ call it safsal (Hebrew) as the scholars do, or &c. (v. אִיסְטְבָא 2).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 22:3">Kel. XXII, 3</cite> <he>ס׳ שניטל וכ׳</he> a bench (long board) which has lost one of its ends (supports).
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 1:12">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. I, 12</cite> <he>ס׳ שנתפרק</he> a frame which has fallen apart.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:33">Y. Ber. IV, 7ᵈ</cite> top <he>שמנים ס׳ היו שם של וכ׳</he> eighty benches (forms) of students were there. Tosef. l. c. 11 <he>הס׳ שבפונדקאות</he> the (movable) benches in inns; <he>הס׳ של מלמדי וכ׳</he> the school teachers’ benches (open frames serving as foot-rests for those behind).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 22:10">Kel. XXII, 10</cite> <he>ס׳ שבמרחץ</he> (used as singular) the (marble) board-frame (with wooden supports).

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 4:6">B. Bath. IV, 6</cite> <he>לא מכר … הס׳</he> (Babli ed. 67ᵇ <he>הסְפָלִין</he>) has not sold (with the bath-house) the boards of the seats. Ib. 67ᵇ <he>בית הס׳</he> Ms. H. a. R. (ed. <he>הספלים</he>) the room where the seats are kept.
<cite ref="Pesachim 51a:5">Pes. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>סַפְסַלֵּי נכרים</he> the frames on which gentiles spread their goods.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 104b:13">Snh. 104ᵇ</cite> <he>לחכה אש בסַפְסִילֵיהֶן</he> (some ed. <he>בסַפְסַלֵּיהָם</he>). fire lapped their benches; a. fr.
